flawed_step: 0024: The claim that separately 3-colouring \overline{G} and \partial G suffices to 3-colour G is unjustified; the colourings need not be compatible across connecting edges.
counterexample: Let the whole graph be K4 on vertices a,b,c,d. Let H1=K4-cd and H2=K4-ab. Then H1 is 3-colourable by a=1,b=2,c=d=3, and H2 is 3-colourable by a=b=1,c=2,d=3. Their union is K4, which requires four colours because every pair of vertices is adjacent. Thus two parts being individually 3-colourable does not imply that their union is 3-colourable.
assessment_summary: The first definitive failure is line 0024. Separate 3-colourability supplies no common colouring agreeing on shared vertices and respecting edges between the parts, so it cannot establish that G is 3-colourable.
